name: THOSE WERE THE DAYS
clue: Sunk in a worn armchair in Queens, Carroll O'Connor played this grumbling loudmouth who called his son-in-law 'Meathead'

name: BLINK & YOU'LL MISS HIM
clue: This portly English director tucked a brief walk-on for himself into dozens of his own thrillers, from 'Rear Window' to 'Psycho'

name: PLAY IT BY EAR
clue: Blind since childhood, this piano man in dark glasses had a 1960 hit that later became the official song of his native Georgia

name: THE GOLDEN DOOR
clue: From 1892 to 1954, some 12 million newcomers to America were processed at this immigration station in New York Harbor

name: RIVETING STUFF
clue: Nevada tailor Jacob Davis took his riveted-pants idea to this San Francisco dry goods merchant, and their 1873 patent gave us blue jeans

name: SUMMERS WITHOUT FEAR
clue: Asked who held the patent on his 1955 polio vaccine, this doctor answered, 'Could you patent the sun?'

name: MERMAID MIX-UP
clue: Columbus took these whiskered, slow-moving grazers for mermaids; they still crowd into Florida's warm springs each winter

name: PIONEER GIRL
clue: A log cabin in Wisconsin, a covered wagon and a Dakota claim shanty all turn up in her 'Little House' books

name: NEWSSTAND NOSTALGIA
clue: Small-town America filled this illustrator's hundreds of Saturday Evening Post covers and his wartime 'Four Freedoms' paintings

name: TEE FOR TWO
clue: A loyal 'Army' of fans followed this Latrobe, Pennsylvania golfer, whose name graces a mix of iced tea and lemonade

name: V FOR VICTORY
clue: Cigar in hand, this British prime minister rallied his nation in 1940 with a vow to fight on the beaches and never surrender

name: THE LADY WHO NEVER WAS
clue: A Minneapolis flour company dreamed up this friendly kitchen expert in 1921 to sign its answers to bakers' letters
